column1: # Independent position map, barnes_scan149.jpg; source pixels origin upper left, 2008x1491.
# Each row is one visually separable mark where possible, or a hole of unknown length.
# Coordinates are approximate centers (typically +/- 6 px; margin +/- 15 px). Segmentation is provisional.
# Reading order: increasing x in horizontal rows, increasing y in counterclockwise-rotated margin rows.
# Descriptors are visual shapes, not equivalences or decipherments. `hole` does not imply one sign.
# H0 is the possible group at right end of the line above H1; cursive flanks it.
# H1 is the long horizontal cipher line, roughly source y 735-760, immediately followed by cursive.
# H2 is the next horizontal embedded sequence, roughly source y 767-790, with cursive on either side.
# H3 is the small underlined candidate below a deletion, roughly x 1340-1460, y 848-867; it is too obscured for segmentation.
# M1 is a marginal line around source x 1215-1230; cursive directly precedes and follows it. Its coordinates are source y, not the x coordinate of the rotated view.
# M2 is another marginal line around source x 1140-1160, between cursive flanks. The large looped boxed shape after 2 is crossed by handwriting and is not assigned a sign.
# M3 is an isolated square-with-dot on the M2 line, after the following cursive. It is a possible cipher mark; role unproven.

# Some glyphs overlap fine interlinear writing. Coordinates and segmentation are estimates, not exact bounding boxes; spans and group boundaries may shift. Marginal rotation exposed new candidates, superseding the earlier statement that no marginal run was confidently segmented.
# AI agents did this work; no person has checked it.
